question: What is the annual benefit maximum per person under the Essential plan?
reference_answer: 500,000 units per insured person per policy year.

evidence.quote: an annual benefit maximum of 500,000 units per insured person per policy year

question: When does a family stop paying individual deductibles on the Essential plan?
reference_answer: Once the combined eligible expenses of all insured members reach 15,000 units in the policy year, no further individual deductible applies to any member.

evidence.quote: A family covered under a single policy satisfies its deductible obligation once the combined eligible expenses of all insured members reach 15,000 units in the policy year, after which no further individual deductible applies to any member.

question: What share of an out-of-network bill does Aurora pay on the Essential plan?
reference_answer: 55 per cent of the allowed amount.

evidence.quote: For out-of-network providers Aurora pays 55 per cent of the allowed amount

question: Does balance billing count toward the Essential plan out-of-pocket maximum?
reference_answer: No. The Essential out-of-pocket maximum is 40,000 units per person, and premiums, balance billing and pre-authorisation penalties do not accrue toward it.

evidence.quote: The annual out-of-pocket maximum under the Essential plan is 40,000 units per person.
Premiums, balance billing and penalties for missed pre-authorisation do not.

question: What happens if an Essential member chooses a private room that is not medically necessary?
reference_answer: Aurora reimburses only the semi-private rate and the member pays the difference.

evidence.quote: Where a member elects a private room without medical necessity, Aurora reimburses the semi-private rate and the difference is borne by the member.

question: How many physiotherapy sessions does each plan allow per year?
reference_answer: Twenty sessions per policy year on Essential and sixty on Premier.

evidence.quote: Physiotherapy is limited to twenty sessions per policy year under the Essential plan.
Physiotherapy is limited to sixty sessions per policy year under the Premier plan.

question: On the Essential plan, how is a branded drug covered when a generic version exists?
reference_answer: It is covered at 60 per cent.

evidence.quote: Branded medicines with an available generic equivalent are covered at 60 per cent.

question: Does the Essential plan pay for fillings and crowns?
reference_answer: No. Restorative dental work is not covered under the Essential plan.

evidence.quote: Restorative dental work is not covered under the Essential plan.

question: What orthodontic cover does the Premier plan provide?
reference_answer: 50 per cent for insured persons under nineteen, up to a lifetime maximum of 60,000 units.

evidence.quote: Orthodontic treatment is covered at 50 per cent for insured persons under the age of nineteen, to a lifetime maximum of 60,000 units.

question: Can a parent stay overnight with an admitted child under the Premier plan?
reference_answer: Yes. One accompanying parent or guardian of an insured child under fourteen is covered for bed and board for the admission, up to 1,200 units per night.

evidence.quote: A single accompanying parent or guardian of an insured child under the age of fourteen is covered for bed and board for the duration of the admission, to a maximum of 1,200 units per night.

question: How long does Premier emergency cover last on a trip abroad?
reference_answer: Emergency treatment abroad is covered at 90 per cent for the first ninety days of a single trip, after which cover ceases for that trip.

evidence.quote: Emergency treatment outside the country of residence is covered at 90 per cent for the first ninety days of any single trip, after which cover ceases for that trip regardless of the member's reason for remaining abroad.

question: How are generic medicines covered on the Premier plan?
reference_answer: They are covered in full.

evidence.quote: Generic medicines are covered in full.

question: Is reconstructive surgery after an accident excluded as cosmetic surgery?
reference_answer: No, provided it follows an accident or a covered surgical procedure and begins within twenty-four months of it.

evidence.quote: unless it is reconstructive surgery following an accident or a covered surgical procedure and is begun within twenty-four months of that accident or procedure

question: Are motor racing injuries covered?
reference_answer: No. Injuries sustained in professional sport or in motor racing of any kind are excluded.

evidence.quote: Treatment of injuries sustained while taking part in professional sport, or while participating in motor racing of any kind.

question: Can a member be treated by a relative who is a doctor?
reference_answer: Only if Aurora has given written consent in advance of the treatment; otherwise it is excluded.

evidence.quote: Treatment delivered by a provider who is a member of the insured person's immediate family is excluded unless Aurora has given written consent in advance of the treatment.

question: An Essential member chips a tooth in a fall and starts treatment two months later. Is it covered?
reference_answer: Yes. Accident-related dental treatment begun within ninety days of the accident is covered at 80 per cent, overriding the Essential exclusion of restorative dental work.

evidence.quote: Dental treatment arising from an accident is excluded under the Essential plan unless the treatment begins within ninety days of the accident, in which case it is covered at 80 per cent notwithstanding the Essential plan's exclusion of restorative dental work.

question: Under what conditions is bariatric surgery covered?
reference_answer: When the member has a body mass index of 35 or above and has completed a documented six-month supervised programme, it is covered at the plan's standard inpatient rate.

evidence.quote: Weight management treatment is excluded unless the member has a body mass index of 35 or above and has completed a documented six-month supervised programme, in which case bariatric surgery is covered at the plan's standard inpatient rate.

question: If a member submits a fraudulent claim, are their earlier settled claims clawed back?
reference_answer: No. The fraudulent claim is declined in full and benefits paid on it become repayable if the policy is cancelled, but unrelated claims settled before that date are not reopened.

evidence.quote: A claim found to be fraudulent is declined in full.
Claims unrelated to the fraud that were settled before that date are not reopened.

question: What is the penalty for notifying Aurora of an admission late?
reference_answer: Notification is due within forty-eight hours. Late notification does not void the claim, but Aurora may reduce the settlement by 10 per cent where the delay prevented it from managing the cost of the episode.

evidence.quote: A member must notify Aurora of an inpatient admission within forty-eight hours of the admission
Aurora may reduce the settlement by 10 per cent of the eligible amount where late notification has prevented it from managing the cost of the episode.

question: How long does a member have to submit a claim?
reference_answer: One hundred and eighty days from the date of treatment, extended to three hundred and sixty-five days where the member shows submission was prevented by circumstances beyond their control.

evidence.quote: A completed claim must reach Aurora within one hundred and eighty days of the date of treatment.
Aurora will consider a claim received within three hundred and sixty-five days of the date of treatment

question: What happens to a claim submitted with an invoice showing only a total amount?
reference_answer: It is returned to the member rather than declined, and the submission deadline is suspended from the date it is returned until the member resubmits it.

evidence.quote: An invoice that states only a total amount without itemisation will be returned to the member rather than declined, and the submission deadline is suspended from the date Aurora returns the invoice until the date the member resubmits it.

question: How quickly is a claim settled, and what happens if Aurora asks for more information?
reference_answer: A complete claim is settled within thirty days of receipt, and the thirty-day period restarts when the last outstanding item is received.

evidence.quote: A complete claim is settled within thirty days of receipt.
the thirty-day period restarts on the date the last outstanding item is received

question: Does Aurora pay interest on late settlements?
reference_answer: Yes, at 6 per cent per annum on settlements paid more than sixty days after a complete claim was received, calculated from the sixty-first day.

evidence.quote: Interest accrues on any settlement paid later than sixty days after a complete claim was received, at a rate of 6 per cent per annum calculated from the sixty-first day.

question: Which exchange rate applies to a foreign-currency invoice?
reference_answer: The central bank rate for the policy currency on the date of treatment, not the date of payment.

evidence.quote: Aurora applies the exchange rate published by the central bank of the policy currency on the date of treatment, not the date of payment.

question: How does Aurora split a cost when the member has other insurance?
reference_answer: It pays a proportionate share based on the ratio of its own annual benefit maximum to the combined annual maxima of all policies in force.

evidence.quote: Aurora pays its proportionate share based on the ratio of its own annual benefit maximum to the combined annual maxima of all policies in force.

question: Do scans need pre-authorisation?
reference_answer: Yes, magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography and positron emission tomography scans all require written pre-authorisation.

evidence.quote: magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography and positron emission tomography scans

question: Above what cost does a course of treatment require pre-authorisation?
reference_answer: Any single course of treatment with an estimated cost above 50,000 units.

evidence.quote: any single course of treatment whose estimated cost exceeds 50,000 units

question: How fast does Aurora answer an urgent pre-authorisation request?
reference_answer: Within twenty-four hours when the physician marks it urgent, against three working days for a standard complete request.

evidence.quote: Aurora responds to a complete request within three working days, or within twenty-four hours where the physician marks the request as urgent.

question: How long does a pre-authorisation stay valid?
reference_answer: Ninety days from the date of issue, after which it lapses and a fresh request is needed.

evidence.quote: An approval is valid for ninety days from the date of issue.

question: What if the final cost exceeds the authorised amount?
reference_answer: An excess of more than 15 per cent over the authorised maximum requires a separate request and may be declined.

evidence.quote: where the final cost exceeds that amount by more than 15 per cent, the excess requires a separate request and may be declined

question: What is the penalty for skipping a required pre-authorisation?
reference_answer: The eligible amount is reduced by 30 per cent before the deductible and coinsurance are applied, and that penalty does not count toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

evidence.quote: Aurora reduces the eligible amount by 30 per cent before applying the deductible and coinsurance.
This penalty does not accrue toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

question: If one hospital stay produces four invoices, how many times is the pre-authorisation penalty applied?
reference_answer: Once. The reduction applies once per episode of care, not once per invoice.

evidence.quote: A reduction under this section is applied once per episode of care, not once per invoice arising from that episode.

question: What is covered if a member goes ahead after a pre-authorisation is declined?
reference_answer: Nothing. The member bears the full cost, and the 30 per cent reduction does not apply because no benefit is payable at all.

evidence.quote: Proceeding with treatment after a request has been declined means the full cost is borne by the member; the 30 per cent reduction does not apply because no benefit is payable at all.

question: What is the waiting period for a pre-existing condition?
reference_answer: Twenty-four months.

evidence.quote: | Pre-existing conditions | twenty-four months |

question: Which procedures count as specified surgical procedures?
reference_answer: Hernia repair, cataract extraction, joint replacement, tonsillectomy and surgical treatment of haemorrhoids.

evidence.quote: Specified surgical procedures are hernia repair, cataract extraction, joint replacement, tonsillectomy and the surgical treatment of haemorrhoids.

question: Does time served with a previous insurer count toward Aurora waiting periods?
reference_answer: Yes, where the break in cover was not more than thirty days, credit is given for time served for benefits the previous policy also covered, and evidence must be provided within sixty days of transfer.

evidence.quote: A member transferring to Aurora from another insurer without a break in cover of more than thirty days receives credit for time already served under the previous policy
Evidence of prior cover must be provided within sixty days of the transfer.

question: What level of cover applies while an upgraded member is still serving the Premier waiting period?
reference_answer: The member is covered at the Essential level until the Premier waiting period for that benefit is served, and at the Premier level thereafter.

evidence.quote: the member is covered at the Essential level until the Premier waiting period for that benefit has been served, and at the Premier level thereafter

question: What happens to waiting periods if a lapsed policy is reinstated after three weeks?
reference_answer: No new waiting period applies and cover is treated as continuous, but treatment received during the lapsed interval is never covered.

evidence.quote: Where cover lapses for non-payment and is reinstated within forty-five days, no new waiting period applies and cover is treated as continuous, but treatment received during the lapsed interval is never covered.

question: Is there a waiting period for a newborn?
reference_answer: No, provided the member adds the child to the policy within thirty days of the birth.

evidence.quote: A child born to an insured member is covered from birth with no waiting period, provided the member adds the child to the policy within thirty days of the birth.

question: Can a member get cashless treatment at a Tier Two hospital?
reference_answer: No. Tier Two hospitals do not support direct settlement, so the member pays and claims reimbursement at the in-network coinsurance rate.

evidence.quote: Tier Two hospitals have agreed tariffs but do not support direct settlement, so the member pays and claims reimbursement at the in-network coinsurance rate.

question: How is the allowed amount set when no Tier One tariff exists for a procedure?
reference_answer: It is the invoiced charge reduced by 25 per cent.

evidence.quote: Where no Tier One tariff exists for the procedure code, the allowed amount is the invoiced charge reduced by 25 per cent.

question: How is an emergency admission to a hospital outside the network reimbursed?
reference_answer: At the in-network rate for the first seventy-two hours, and beyond that if the treating clinician certifies in writing that transfer is unsafe.

evidence.quote: An emergency admission to any hospital is reimbursed at the in-network rate for the first seventy-two hours.
Where the treating clinician certifies in writing that transfer is unsafe, the in-network rate continues to apply for the remainder of the admission.

question: What happens to an authorisation if the hospital leaves the network?
reference_answer: It remains honoured at the in-network rate for ninety days after the removal takes effect.

evidence.quote: the authorisation remains honoured at the in-network rate for ninety days after the removal takes effect

question: Does the Essential plan cover maternity?
reference_answer: No. Maternity cover is Premier only; Essential covers complications of pregnancy as a general illness but not routine antenatal care or an uncomplicated delivery.

evidence.quote: Maternity cover is provided under the Premier plan only.
The Essential plan covers complications of pregnancy as a general illness but does not cover routine antenatal care or an uncomplicated delivery.

question: Is the maternity waiting period measured to conception or to delivery?
reference_answer: To the date of delivery, not the date of conception or of the first antenatal appointment.

evidence.quote: The waiting period is measured to the date of delivery, not to the date of conception or the date of the first antenatal appointment.

question: How much is covered for an elective caesarean compared with a medically indicated one?
reference_answer: An elective caesarean without clinical indication is covered up to 180,000 units, the same as an uncomplicated vaginal delivery, while a medically indicated caesarean is covered up to 320,000 units.

evidence.quote: An elective caesarean section requested without clinical indication is covered up to the same 180,000 units, with any excess borne by the member.
A medically indicated caesarean section is covered up to 320,000 units.

question: Is an emergency caesarean during labour subject to the delivery limit?
reference_answer: No. It is treated as a complication rather than a delivery, so it falls under the inpatient benefit instead.

evidence.quote: a caesarean section performed in response to an emergent complication during labour is treated as a complication and not as a delivery

question: What cover does a newborn have before being added to the policy?
reference_answer: Automatic cover from birth for thirty days under the mother's policy with no separate premium, limited to 150,000 units.

evidence.quote: A newborn child is covered from birth for thirty days under the mother's policy without a separate premium
This automatic cover is limited to 150,000 units.

question: Is IVF covered?
reference_answer: No. Assisted reproduction, including in vitro fertilisation and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, is excluded under every plan.

evidence.quote: Assisted reproduction, including in vitro fertilisation and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, is not covered under any plan.

question: How long does a member have to appeal a declined claim?
reference_answer: Ninety days from the date of the decision letter.

evidence.quote: A member may appeal a declined claim or a declined pre-authorisation within ninety days of the date of the decision letter.

question: How quickly is an appeal handled when treatment is time sensitive?
reference_answer: Within seventy-two hours for an appeal against a declined pre-authorisation where treatment is time sensitive.

evidence.quote: For an appeal against a declined pre-authorisation where treatment is time sensitive, Aurora responds within seventy-two hours.

question: Is the Ombudsman's decision binding on the member?
reference_answer: No. It binds Aurora but not the member.

evidence.quote: The Ombudsman's determination is binding on Aurora and is not binding on the member.

question: Does appealing pause the claim submission deadline?
reference_answer: Yes. An internal appeal suspends the one-hundred-and-eighty-day deadline for the claim under appeal, from receipt of the appeal until the outcome letter.

evidence.quote: Submitting an internal appeal suspends the one-hundred-and-eighty-day claim submission deadline in respect of the claim under appeal.

question: Does filing a grievance extend a claim deadline?
reference_answer: No. A grievance does not pause any deadline applying to a claim or an appeal.

evidence.quote: A grievance does not pause any deadline that applies to a claim or an appeal.

question: A day procedure runs past midnight. Is it still a day case?
reference_answer: No. An admission extending past midnight is an inpatient admission regardless of its planned duration.

evidence.quote: An admission that extends past midnight is an inpatient admission regardless of its planned duration.

question: How far back does Aurora look when deciding if a condition is pre-existing?
reference_answer: Thirty-six months before the cover start date, covering treatment, prescribed medication or a diagnosis.

evidence.quote: Any condition for which the member received treatment, took prescribed medication, or was given a diagnosis in the thirty-six months before the cover start date.

question: If treatment is medically necessary, must Aurora cover it?
reference_answer: No. A treatment may be medically necessary and still be excluded.

evidence.quote: A treatment may be medically necessary and still be excluded.

question: Is a repetitive strain injury treated as an accident?
reference_answer: No. A condition developing gradually from repeated activity is not an accident, even if the member can identify when symptoms began.

evidence.quote: A condition that develops gradually as a result of repeated activity is not an accident, even where the member can identify the moment the symptoms began.

question: Are annual benefit limits pro-rated for someone joining mid-year?
reference_answer: No. Per-policy-year limits reset on each anniversary and are not pro-rated.

evidence.quote: Benefit limits expressed per policy year reset on each anniversary and are not pro-rated where a member joins mid-year.

question: Does an ambulance transfer between hospitals eat into the annual benefit maximum?
reference_answer: No. A medically necessary transfer is covered in full under the Emergency Transport benefit, and amounts paid under that benefit do not count toward the annual benefit maximum.

evidence.quote: The cost of a medically necessary transfer between hospitals is covered in full under the Emergency Transport benefit and does not count toward the annual benefit maximum.
Amounts paid under the Emergency Transport benefit do not count toward the annual benefit maximum.

question: What is the monthly premium for the Aurora Premier plan?
reference_answer: The provided documents do not state premium amounts.

question: Does Aurora cover acupuncture sessions?
reference_answer: The provided documents do not mention acupuncture.

question: Which hospitals are in Tier One in the northern region?
reference_answer: The provided documents describe the tier system but do not list individual hospitals.

question: What is Aurora's customer service telephone number?
reference_answer: The provided documents do not give contact details.

question: Does the Essential plan pay for hearing aids?
reference_answer: The provided documents do not mention hearing aids.
